<strong>Emmy Noether</strong> demostró e: Emmy Noether proved in 1918 the theorem that links symmetry with physics: to each symmetry of a system there corresponds a quantity that is conserved. That the laws do not change with time implies that energy is conserved; that they do not change on shifting position, that momentum is conserved. She was also one of the founders of abstract algebra, the way of studying groups and other structures by their properties and not by their elements. In Göttingen she taught for years without a salary and under David Hilbert's name, because the university would not accept women lecturers. When she died, in 1935, Einstein wrote that she had been the most significant creative mathematical genius since women gained access to higher education.
